events.title: Rwanda restriction at Gatuna and on travel to Uganda
events.scope: Gatuna/Katuna crossing; broader restrictions on Rwandan travel to Uganda
events.crossings: Gatuna/Katuna; selective-permission reporting also names Kagitumba/Mirama Hills, where its detailed interview is situated. Cyanika evidence is contextual, not a claim that every phase applied at every gate.
events.direction: Rwandan exit to Uganda especially restricted; practical effects on both directions.
events.movement: Traders, cargo and passengers; resumption initially prioritised cargo and returnees.
events.exceptions: Foreigners crossed during 2019 Rwandan departure denials. January 2020 reporting describes selective accepted-reason permission. January 2022 inward cargo, citizens and returning residents were exceptions. Later bus and local-ID travel had different conditions.
events.enforcement: Reuters, AFP and Anadolu report limited observed crossings on 31 January.
events.status_observation: Partial reopening observed 2022-01-31
events.official_rationale: Initial RRA heavy-truck diversion officially cited construction; later reclosure reporting cites structural cracks through an unnamed officer. Rwanda also alleged harassment of nationals and Ugandan support for dissidents, which Uganda disputed. These explanations belong to different accounts and should not be collapsed. Contemporary officials called the passenger warning advisory and attributed it to alleged insecurity; enforcement is separately documented. COVID explains stated 2022 exceptions and testing; national policy is GL04.
events.context: Diplomatic dispute; reopening followed bilateral contacts and Muhoozi Kainerugaba visit.
events.uncertainty: Passenger denial is documented by March 1, 2019; exact first onset remains unresolved. Dated denials and selective permissions do not establish a continuous 2019–2022 all-traffic closure. Preserve February 28 freight diversion, June 10–22 truck trial, January 31, 2022 cargo/returnee permission, March 7 outgoing bus and later local-shopping relaxation as different scopes. Freight eligibility remains contested; national COVID policy is GL04.

events.title: Burundi COVID entry restriction from Rwanda
events.scope: Burundi–Rwanda land border, Ruhwa specifically corroborated
events.movement: Passengers arriving from Rwanda, including Congolese transit travellers and schoolchildren.
events.exceptions: Air passengers reported continuing on 15 March. Cargo policy differed by phase: The New Times reported restored cargo movement on 13 April 2020, while IWACU reports a foreign-ministry note dated 14 April. Neither fixes a passenger reopening.
events.imposing_authority: Burundian immigration authorities implementing reported verbal order
events.enforcement: Contemporaneous testimony in SOS and Radio Okapi reports denied passenger entry. Formal written Burundi order not retrieved; source independence is not assumed merely from publisher count.
events.status_observation: Observed restriction 2020-03-15
events.official_rationale: Response to first reported COVID-19 cases in Rwanda.
events.uncertainty: Distinct tightening within earlier political restrictions GL02; no separate reopening date established. Avoid double-counting simultaneous causes as additional full closures. Later freight restrictions were uneven: an IWACU account of Rwanda’s 30 March note reports blocked trucks and admissions at different posts. Another IWACU report describes a 14 April goods-vehicle relaxation. Neither identifies the separate passenger endpoint. An opened New Times report dated 13 April 2020 already describes resumed cargo movement through government/FEAFFA statements. Keep this earlier reporting distinct from the 14 April note reported by IWACU; exact implementation across crossings remains unresolved. A substantially matching Egypt SIS indexed article displayed as 28 June 2022 is not evidence of a separate 2022 episode.

events.title: Burundi restrictions on Rwanda border following political crisis
events.scope: Burundi–Rwanda land frontier
events.crossings: Ruhwa; Kanyaru-Haut/Akanyaru Haut; Gasenyi-Nemba/Nemba (evidence differs by phase).
events.direction: Burundian controls restricted both entry and exit in observed March 2022 cases; no uniform direction established for entire regime.
events.movement: Passenger and small-trader restrictions varied by phase. March 2022 field reporting includes outbound Burundian traders, Burundian returnees and outbound Rwandans; later agency-vehicle transit was permitted.
events.exceptions: Reported agency-vehicle entry/exit permission from Bukavu via Rwanda dated 29 August 2022 (RTNK; original order not retrieved). Burundi Eco issue 521, printed 2 September 2022, more specifically describes an Interior ministry letter of 29 August to the national police inspector general instructing permission for Mapassa Car Transit via Ruhwa for its Congolese and Burundian clients coming from DRC through Rwanda. Burundi Eco 16 September field reporting describes those passengers at Ruhwa. These preceded general ministry-permit relaxation observed 30 September.
events.enforcement: SOS reporters observed 30 September crossing without former ministry permission at Kanyaru-Hautand Ruhwa; Gasenyı-Nemba applied relaxation later that day.
events.status_observation: Partial relaxation observed30September2022; generalreopening acknowledged22/25October.
events.official_rationale: Burundi demanded extradition of people it accused of the 2015 coup attempt.
events.context: Retrospective reports describe a prolonged closure spanning political tensions and COVID restrictions.
events.uncertainty: Onset and continuity unresolved. 2020 traveller reports show earlier selective access. 30 September 2022 is documented relaxation atnamedposts, with one witness hearing opening previous evening. Government still denied formal opening then; ministry acknowledged opening22/25 October. Earlier limited bus transit means 30 September is not the first reopening of every category. 29 August is a reported permission date, not an observed first crossing. Official March 2022 statement supports political context, not a uniform continuous closure. The newly inspected Burundi Eco brief reports the letter but is not the original administrative instrument. UMUSEKE contemporary Kinyarwanda reporting corroborates March 2022 restrictions at Ruhwa; its retrospective 2016 reference does not resolve onset or continuity.
